BiblicalUsage: Ten is the number inside the counting of Israel, and it turns up in fourteens and twelves and eighteens. The Passover lamb is kept until the fourteenth day, Elim has twelve wells of water, Abram arms three hundred and eighteen trained servants, and Ishmael is promised twelve princes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ten is the round number of God's counting: a full set, a complete company, a measure that comes out even. And I hold that the God who counts wells and servants and princes counts His people the same way, and none of the number is lost.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
